summary: Charles Goodman works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan in 2002 under Allan Gibbard and was attested as an associate professor at Binghamton University in 2013.

Charles H. Long was a religious studies scholar who earned his BD (1953) and PhD (1962) from the University of Chicago. He held posts at Chicago, UNC Chapel Hill, Syracuse, Duke, and UC Santa Barbara.

Charles Hallisey is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Colgate, Harvard, UPenn, and the University of Chicago (PhD 1988). He taught at Loyola University Chicago, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and Harvard University.

Charles Hamilton worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He served in the military for the East India Company starting in 1776 and was one of the first members of The Asiatic Society from around 1784 to 1792.

Charles Harris worked in Indology and linguistics. After graduating from Indiana University, he earned a PhD at the University of Leipzig in 1884 under Ernst Windisch. He served as professor of German at Oberlin College and Case Western Reserve University.

Charles Henry Allan Bennett worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He founded the Buddhasasana Samagama and The Buddhist Review, and served as head of the Buddhist Society of Great Britain and Ireland in 1908.

Charles Henry Tawney was an Indologist educated at Trinity College, Cambridge. He served as Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, held professorships and leadership at Presidency University, was Registrar of the University of Calcutta, and was Librarian at the India Office.

Charles Hubert Biddulph was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Philander Smith College and the Crystal Palace School of Engineering. From 1924 to 1966, he worked as an engineer and deputy general manager for the South Indian Railway Company.
Charles Hyart was a linguist who studied at the University of Liège from around 1931 to 1935 under René Fohalle. He later taught Russian at the University of Liège from approximately 1948 to 1983.

Charles James Lyall worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at King's College London and Balliol College, Oxford, served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1867 to 1898, and was professor of Arabic at Oxford from 1913 to 1920.

Charles James Rodgers worked in Indology and history/archaeology after studying at Borough Road College and Cambridge. He served as principal of Amritsar's Christian Vernacular Education Society Training College, honorary numismatist to the Government of India, and Punjab Religious Book Society secretary.

Charles Johnston worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Trinity College Dublin from around 1884 to 1888 and served as a special lecturer in political science at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1908.

Charles Jones Ogden worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Columbia University under A. V. Williams Jackson, earning an AB in 1900, and later served there as honorary lecturer in Indo-Iranian languages (1926–1931).
Charles Lecoutere was a linguist who earned his PhD from KU Leuven in 1892, studying under Charles-Joseph de Harlez de Deulin. He became a professor at KU Leuven in 1895.

Charles Li works in Indology, philosophy, and computational fields. He earned his PhD from the University of Cambridge in 2018, held a postdoctoral fellowship at UBC, was a CNRS researcher, and became Arbeitsstellenleiter at the University of Hamburg in 2023.

Charles Louis Fabri was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who studied at the University of Pécs and Leiden under Jean Philippe Vogel and Sylvain Lévi. He held posts at Leiden, the Archaeological Survey of India, and the Lahore Museum.

Charles Malamoud is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Paris. He taught at the University of Lyon from around 1957 to 1969 and served as Directeur d'Études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from ~1979 to 1998.

Charles Masson was an Indology and history/archaeology researcher who served as an agent for the East India Company from around 1822 to 1826 and for the Government of India from approximately 1835 to 1838.

Charles Matthew Whish worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the East India Company College and the College of Fort St. George, serving as a civil servant in Madras Presidency and for the East India Company from 1812 to 1833.

Charles Michel was a linguist and Indologist who studied at KU Leuven under Félix Nève and the University of Paris under Abel Bergaigne. He held professorships at Ghent University and the University of Liège.
